properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1304269
Incident Time: 2021-05-04 12:24:00
Nearest City: Garden River First Nation, CN
Location: 51 GREEN SKY STREET
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: GASOLINE: AUTOMOTIVE (UNLEADED)
Medium Affected: LAND
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 46.535502, -84.151728 (Approximated from street_address)
Report Description12:07 GARDEN RIVER WATER FACILITY SUPERVISOR FIRST NATION CODY BOISSONIEAU 705-971-1210 TO SAC(HM) REPORTING ON BEHALF OF THE FIRST NATIONS REGARDING A SPILL IN A DITCH LOCATED ON 51 GREEN SKY STREET, GARDEN RIVER FIRST NATION. CALLER SAYS THEY GOT A REPORT FROM THE RESIDENT THAT LIVES AT THIS ADDRESS THAT THEY CAN SMELL GASOLINE IN THEIR HOME LAST FRIDAY. CALLER SAYS THEY CAME TO SITE TODAY AND HAD UNION GAS ATTEND. CALLER SAYS THERE WAS SOME GASOLINE OR SOME TYPE OF POLLUTANT FOUND IN THE SUMP CAUSING FOR THE ODOURS. CALLER SAYS UNION GAS FOUND THERE WERE LEL LEVELS PRESENT. CALLER SAYS THEY HAVE TEMPORARILY REROUTED THE SUMP TO OUTSIDE OF THE BUILDING TO AVOID ANY CONCERNS FOR THE RESIDENT. CALLER SAYS THEY HAD A LOT OF PRECIPITATION IN THE PAST BIT AND BELIEVE A SPILL THAT WAS IN THE DITCH WERE THE CAUSE OF THE SUMP BEING IMPACTED. CALLER SAYS THE DITCHES WATER LEVEL ROSE PAST THE SUMPS DISCHARGE PIPE AND WENT BACK INTO THE HOUSEHOLD CAUSING THE ODOURS AND SUMP IMPACTS. CALLER SAYS THEY BELIEVE THE SPILL IS LIKELY TO HAVE COME FROM A LARGE 5 BAY GARAGE BUILDING NEXT TO THE RESIDENCE. CALLER SAYS THERE IS A FD, EMP BUILDING AND MANY LARGE VEHICLES NEARBY. CALLER SAYS THERE ARE ALSO SNOW TRUCKS AND SUCH WITHIN THE AREA THAT ARE MAINTAINED. CALLER SAYS THEY CANNOT PINPOINT WHERE THE SPILL CAME FROM, BUT THERE IS EVIDENT SPILLAGE TO THE DITCH AREA AND HAS AN OIL/GASOLINE STAIN. CALLER SAYS THE FD WAS MADE AWARE AND SO BOOMS WERE PLACED IN THE DITCH, BUT NO CLEAN-UP HAS COMMENCED. CALLER SAYS THEY HAVE HAD THEIR ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH OFFICER ATTEND SITE AND TAKE SAMPLES. CALLER SAYS THEY ARE LOOKING FOR RECOMMENDATIONS GOING FORWARD BY LOCAL MECP. CALLER SAYS THEY WILL PROVIDE WRITTEN PERMISSION TO ATTEND SITE AND GLADLY PROVIDE MECP ACCESS. CALLER SAYS LOCAL MECP SAULT STE MARIE IS ALREADY AWARE OF THE ISSUE, BUT THEY WERE ASKED TO CALL INTO SAC TO MAKE A REPORT. CALLER WAS INFORMED REPORT WILL BE SENT TO LOCAL MECP AND ECCC.

THIS EVENT DID NOT OCCUR AS A RESULT OF A BRAKE FAILURE INCIDENT AND EMPLOYEES ON THE TRAIN WILL BE DRUG AND ALCOHOL TESTED. THE TRAIN AND TRACK SPEED WERE UNKNOWN TO THE CALLER AND THIS DID NOT OCCUR AT A GRADE CROSSING.

APPROXIMATELY 20 GALLONS (158 POUNDS) OF NATURAL GAS ODORANT, OR METHYL MERCAPTAN SPILLED BECAUSE OF A FAULTY PIPE UNION. ATMOS PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT THE SITE AT APPROXIMATELY 2:00 A.M. ON THE MORNING OF AUGUST 7 BECAUSE OF CONTINUED COMPLAINTS OF ODOR COMING FROM THE SITE. ATMOS PERSONNEL AGAIN RESPONDED TO THE SITE AND REPLACED THE FAULTY UNION WHICH PERMANENTLY STOPPED THE LEAK.

APPROXIMATELY 20 GALLONS (158 POUNDS) OF NATURAL GAS ODORANT, OR METHYL MERCAPTAN SPILLED BECAUSE OF A FAULTY PIPE UNION. ATMOS PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT THE SITE AT APPROXIMATELY 2:00 A.M. AND TIGHTENED THE UNION WHICH STOPPED THE LEAK. ATMOS PERSONNEL WERE AGAIN CALLED TO THE SITE AT APPROXIMATELY 8:00 A.M. ON THE MORNING OF AUGUST 7 BECAUSE OF CONTINUED COMPLAINTS OF ODOR COMING FROM THE SITE. ATMOS PERSONNEL AGAIN RESPONDED TO THE SITE AND REPLACED THE FAULTY UNION WHICH PERMANENTLY STOPPED THE LEAK.

properties.content:

Nearest City: Honolulu, HI
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: UNKNOWN OIL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: ROBINSON CONSTRUCTION
Skytruth Analysis
APPROXIMATELY 1 GALLON OF PETROLEUM-CONTAMINATED GROUNDWATER WAS RELEASED TO A STORM DRAIN INLET ON PACIFIC STREET DURING CONSTRUCTION DEWATERING. DURING EXCAVATION OF A UTILITY CORRIDOR ON PACIFIC STREET, DEWATERING WAS BEING CONDUCTED. A DUMP TRUCK DROVE OVER A 2-INCH DIAMENTER DISCHARGE HOSE CAUSING THE HOSE TO RUPTURE. A RELEASE OF PETROLEUM-CONTAMINATED GROUNDWATER ONTO THE STREET OCCURRED FOR APPROXIMATELY 10 SECONDS BEFORE THE PUMP WAS TURNED OFF. FREE PRODUCT WAS VISIBLE ON THE GROUNDWATER IN THE EXCAVATION, BUT PETROLEUM-ABSORBENT PADS WERE USED TO PREVENT THE FREE PRODUCT FROM BEING REMOVED FROM THE EXCAVATION IN THE DEWATERING WATER. GUTTER BUDDIES WERE INSTALLED IN THE STORM DRAINS ALONG PACIFIC STREET BEFORE THE INCIDENT OCCURRED. ALL BUT APPROXIMATELY 1-GALLON OF PETROLEUM-CONTAMINATED GROUNDWATER THAT WAS RELEASED ONTO PACIFIC STREET WAS DIVERTED BACK INTO THE EXCAVATION.
